input.quote: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) ends at limb (g) with use covenants only and confers no right on Garman to audit licence compliance, count copies or access Sparkling systems; Section 20 (General Matters) covers only time of the essence and notices; and searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "monitor", "premises", "remote" and "records" return no audit-type right binding us. The only examination right in the document runs in our favour (Section 16 escrow: Sparkling may itself or through independent experts examine and test the deposited materials for Garman's compliance). The single Sparkling-side verification obligation is the narrow post-termination self-certification of destruction/return in Section 17(b), which involves no Garman inspection, entry or system access and so does not engage this rule's frequency, notice or cost parameters. Because there is no Vendor audit right at all, the position is better than preferred on every material term (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access), so no redline is warranted; inserting audit language would create exposure we do not presently have. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to constrain.
